Design System · v3

Money that moves as fast as a message.

Seti turns a WhatsApp thread into a settlement rail — stablecoins in, mobile money out, nothing lost in between. This system keeps every surface, from a quote card to a status update, speaking with the same voice.

01 — Principles

What this brand has to be true to

These aren't values off a poster — they're constraints that came directly out of building the product. Every visual and verbal choice in this system should trace back to one of these.

State the truth, not the hope

A confirmation on one chain isn't a payout. We show progress as progress and never round a pending transfer up to "done."

One thread, not one app

The whole product fits inside a conversation. Nothing in this system should ask someone to leave WhatsApp to understand what happened to their money.

Borderless by default

A quote works the same whether the recipient is across town or across a border. The design doesn't add ceremony to something that should feel ordinary.

Show your work

Every transfer carries a reference, a hash, a receipt. Data that proves what happened is never hidden behind a friendlier-sounding message.

02 — Voice

Concise, transactional, reassuring under uncertainty

People are moving real money inside a chat window. Clarity beats friendliness — but clarity delivered coldly reads as a system that doesn't care whether the money arrived.

Avoid
"Your transaction is being processed by our sophisticated verification pipeline."
Instead
"Your swap and transfer both confirmed — we're just waiting on the final payout now."
Avoid
"ERR_IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH: duplicate key rejected."
Instead
"That confirmation code has already been used — no charge was made twice."
03 — Logo

The mark and the wordmark, always together on first use

The globe is a wireframe sphere, not a solid icon — it should always read as structure you can see through, echoing the ledger underneath every transfer. Minimum clear space around the lockup equals the height of the globe mark itself.

04 — Colour

Sampled from the mark, not chosen from a wheel

The core palette is the exact gradient the logo already uses. We don't introduce new brand hues to "warm up" a screen — restraint here is what keeps a payments product feeling calm rather than promotional.

Status colour — tied to the state machine, not decoration

These four colours map directly onto transactions.status. A colour is only ever used to mean one of these four things, anywhere in the product.

In progress

Swap, transfer, or payout underway.

SWAPPING · PRETIUM_VERIFYING

Settled

Payout confirmed by the provider.

COMPLETED

Needs attention

Ambiguous — escalated, not lost.

MANUAL_REVIEW · *_UNKNOWN

Reversed

Refunded automatically, no user action needed.

SAGA_COMPENSATED
05 — Typography

Outfit for voice, mono for proof

Outfit carries every headline, label, and message — it's geometric and rounded enough to match the mark's own terminals. IBM Plex Mono is used only for the things that need to be copied exactly: hashes, references, quote IDs.

06 — Iconography

One stroke weight, always open

Icons are line-drawn at a consistent 1.6px stroke, never filled solid — the same "wireframe, not solid" logic as the globe mark. No emoji stand in for a system icon; emoji are reserved for conversational warmth in chat copy only.

08 — Spacing

An 8px scale, nothing in between

Every margin and padding in the product traces to this scale. It keeps a hand-built WhatsApp message and a future dashboard screen feeling like the same rhythm.

09 — Ground rules

Fast to check, hard to get wrong

Do

  • Show a transaction ID or hash any time money moves.
  • Say "confirmed" only once the backend has confirmed it.
  • Use the four status colours consistently — never invent a fifth.
  • Keep the globe mark as open wireframe, never filled.

Don't

  • Show an internal error code or state name to a user.
  • Add a new accent colour to make a screen feel "more done."
  • Round an in-progress transfer up to "complete."
  • Use a solid-fill icon anywhere in the product.
